meta.expect: After Hale owns the procedural mistake she gives a small sign of ground (a flat 'Okay', uses Hale's name, writes it down) but does not give up her position on the essay.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale. Owen's zero, who decided it, and why did I find out from a gradebook instead of a phone call?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. My school's procedure says I should have called first. I was wrong, and I've asked the office to note that.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now the zero itself: on what basis did you enter it?
I still have a real concern about the essay itself, and I'd like to show you why.
Then show me, Hale. I'm writing as you go.
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in the play. Here is the scene; you can read it.
I'm reading it, and I'm writing down Act 3, Scene 2. A line quoted wrongly in Owen's essay costs him marks for accuracy, not the whole essay. What else do you have?
